title: Registry Keys and File Security areas: ACL propagation codes and SDDL payloads
blocked_reason: The security-template-secedit lane requires member-ws2025-disposable (pending-qualification): the open WP-3 PR-19 follow-up forbids expanding the lane beyond the certified account/audit/user-rights tranche on the shared host.

provenance.note: Shape derived from Microsoft security-template documentation. Propagation code meanings in particular are asserted from documentation, not captured behavior, and the first secedit /export capture must confirm them before any claim.

anchors.note: Certified WP-3 tranche evidence; proves the harness mechanics this scenario reuses, not these areas.

operator_meaning: Audit key: propagate inheritable permissions, full control to administrators
Locked key: protect against replacement, administrators full, authenticated users read
Data directory: replace existing permissions with the authored set
ReadOnly directory: protect against replacement, read for authenticated users

derivations: Each entry is quoted-path, numeric propagation code, quoted SDDL. Documented code meanings: 0 = propagate inheritable permissions to subkeys/subfolders, 1 = replace existing permissions, 2 = do not allow permissions to be replaced. These meanings are spec-informed until the first capture.
Registry paths use the MACHINE\ hive prefix form in security templates, not HKLM; file paths are absolute local paths. Both are quoted CSV fields.
Studio's security_template.py has no typed accessor for either area; entries parse as opaque lines under known section names. The wire truth fixed here is what a typed model must honor.

open_questions: Does secedit /export emit the same propagation codes it accepted, or normalize (for example, an authored 0 returning as a different code with inherited flags folded into the SDDL)?
Are environment-variable paths (%SystemRoot%) accepted in File Security entries, and how are they returned on export?
What does secedit do with a Registry Keys entry for a key that does not exist at /import time: accept silently, warn, or fail?
